stem: In a vacuum flask, what is the main purpose of the vacuum between the double walls?

options.content: To stop conduction and convection
To stop radiation
options.rationale: Radiation crosses a vacuum; the silvering reduces it.

options.content: To make the flask lighter
To keep the liquid from spilling

explanation: With no particles in the gap, energy cannot be conducted or convected across it.

stem: Why are the inner walls of a vacuum flask silvered?

options.content: To reduce energy transfer by radiation
options.rationale: Correct: shiny surfaces are poor emitters and reflect radiation.

options.content: To stop energy transfer by convection
To make the inside look clean and attractive
To conduct energy away from the drink faster

explanation: Silvered surfaces are poor emitters and good reflectors of infrared, reducing radiation losses.

stem: Match each feature of a vacuum flask with the energy transfer it reduces.

left.content: Insulating pads supporting the inner bottle

right.content: Convection and evaporation through the top

explanation: Each feature tackles a particular method of energy transfer.

stem: Why is the collector panel of a solar water heater painted dull black?

options.content: Black paint stops convection.
Black surfaces reflect sunlight onto the water tank above them.
Black paint insulates the pipes.
Dull black is the best absorber of infrared radiation.

explanation: A dull black surface absorbs the most radiation from the Sun.

stem: In a solar water heater without a pump, why must the storage tank be placed above the collector panel?

options.content: So the tank receives more sunlight on the roof than the panel.
Hot water is denser, so it must be lifted into the tank.
options.rationale: Hot water is less dense; it rises.

options.content: Hot water rises into the tank; cooler water sinks back to the panel.
To make the whole system lighter and easier to fix on the roof.

explanation: The circulation depends on convection: heated, less dense water rises to the tank above.
hints: Does heated water rise or sink?

stem: On a sunny afternoon by Lake Kariba, a breeze blows from the lake towards the land. Why?

options.content: The water is hotter than the land, so air flows from it.
options.rationale: By day the land is hotter.

options.content: Wind always blows from water towards land, day and night.
Land heats faster than water; air over it rises and lake air moves in.
The lake gives out cold radiation that pushes the cooler air inland over the land.

explanation: Land has a lower specific heat capacity and warms faster; warm air rises over the land and air from over the water replaces it.

stem: At night the breeze often blows from the land towards a large lake.
explanation: At night the land cools faster than the water; air rises over the warmer water and air flows from the land: a land breeze.

stem: People sit around a wood fire on a cold evening.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Explain how energy reaches the faces of people sitting beside (not above) the fire.

points.description: By (infrared) radiation from the flames and hot embers

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain why smoke rises above the fire and fresh air flows in at the bottom.

points.description: Hot gases above the fire expand, become less dense and rise (convection)
cooler, denser air flows in at the bottom to replace them

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: A metal poker is left with one end in the fire. Explain why the other end becomes hot.

points.description: Energy is conducted along the metal (by free electrons and vibrating particles) from the hot end to the cool end

explanation: Radiation warms people beside the fire; convection carries hot gases up and draws in fresh air; conduction heats the poker.

stem: In a car's cooling system, how is energy carried from the engine to the radiator?

options.content: By radiation through the air between engine and radiator
Pumped hot water carries the energy round by (forced) convection
By conduction along the walls of the rubber pipes to the front
It is not carried: it is destroyed in the hot engine block

explanation: Water heated by conduction in the engine is pumped to the radiator: the moving water carries the energy (forced convection).
hints: The water moves round the system.

stem: Why do thatched roofs keep huts cool in the day and warm at night?

options.content: Thatch is a good conductor, so heat passes out.
The thatch traps air, which is a poor conductor.
Thatch reflects all the radiation that falls on it.
Thatch produces a little heat at night as it dries.

explanation: The many air pockets in thatch reduce conduction in both directions.
